# List Tickets

## Prerequisites

- Zendesk Support instance access with permission to list/read tickets

## Method

`GET`

## URL

`https://{{OAUTH_REQUEST_PAYLOAD.formData.ZENDESK_SUBDOMAIN}}.zendesk.com/api/v2/tickets`

## Headers

```json
{
  "Accept": "application/json"
}
```

## Description

Returns a list of tickets. Supports filtering by external ID and support type, sorting, sideloading related resources, and both offset- and cursor-based pagination.

## Enforcement Rules

- This endpoint has **no path parameters**.
- When executing the action, ensure to send **Query Parameters** in the URL as query parameters and **not** in the body.
- Pagination: the `page` parameter supports **either**:
  - Traditional pagination: `?page=2` (integer), **or**
  - Cursor pagination using deepObject: `?page[size]=50&page[after]=<cursor>` / `?page[size]=50&page[before]=<cursor>`
  - These are **mutually exclusive**, do **not** use both formats in the same request.

## Optional Query Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `external_id` | string | Lists tickets by external id. External ids don't have to be unique for each ticket; the request may return multiple tickets with the same external id. |
| `sort_by` | string (enum) | Sort by. Possible values: `id`, `subject`, `deleted_at`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, `status`, `requester`, `requester.name`, `group`, `assignee`, `assignee.name`. |
| `sort_order` | string (enum) | Sort order. Possible values: `asc`, `desc`. Default: `asc`. |
| `support_type_scope` | string | Lists tickets by support type. Possible values: `all`, `agent`, `ai_agent`. Default: `agent`. |
| `page` | oneOf (integer \| object) | Pagination parameter. Supports both traditional offset and cursor-based pagination. Traditional: `?page=2`. Cursor (deepObject): `?page[size]=50&page[after]=cursor` or `?page[size]=50&page[before]=cursor`. Mutually exclusive formats. |
| `page[after]` | string | Cursor token for next page (used with cursor pagination). Example: `eyJvIjoiaWQiLCJ2IjoiYVFFPSJ9`. |
| `page[before]` | string | Cursor token for previous page (used with cursor pagination). Example: `eyJvIjoiaWQiLCJ2IjoiYVFFPSJ9`. |
| `page[size]` | integer | Number of records per page (used with cursor pagination). Min: `1`. Example: `50`. |
| `per_page` | integer | Number of records to return per page. Note: default and maximum values vary by endpoint. Example: `50`. |
| `sort` | string | Field to sort results by. Prefix with `-` for descending order. When used with cursor pagination, this determines the cursor ordering. Example: `name` or `-created_at`. |
| `include` | string | Sideloads to include in the response. Comma-separated list. Example: `users,groups,organizations`. |
| `start_time` | integer | Unix epoch time to filter tickets. Only tickets created or updated after this time are returned. Example: `1332034771`. |

## Response

### Success Response (200 OK)

```json
{
  "tickets": [
    {
      "id": 123,
      "subject": "Printer is on fire",
      "description": "The printer in the lobby is smoking.",
      "status": "open",
      "priority": "high",
      "requester_id": 456,
      "assignee_id": 789,
      "group_id": 321,
      "organization_id": 654,
      "external_id": "ext-001",
      "tags": ["hardware", "urgent"],
      "created_at": "2024-01-15T10:30:00Z",
      "updated_at": "2024-01-15T11:00:00Z",
      "url": "https://{{OAUTH_REQUEST_PAYLOAD.formData.ZENDESK_SUBDOMAIN}}.zendesk.com/api/v2/tickets/123.json",
      "via": {
        "channel": "web",
        "source": {}
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

### Error Responses

The scraped content only explicitly documents a `200` response for this endpoint.

## Response Fields

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `tickets` | array | Array of ticket objects. |
| `tickets[].allow_attachments` | boolean | Permission for agents to add add attachments to a comment. Defaults to true. |
| `tickets[].allow_channelback` | boolean | Is false if channelback is disabled, true otherwise. Only applicable for channels framework ticket. |
| `tickets[].assignee_email` | string | Write only. The email address of the agent to assign the ticket to. |
| `tickets[].assignee_id` | integer | The agent currently assigned to the ticket. |
| `tickets[].attribute_value_ids` | array of integer | Write only. IDs of attribute values to associate with the ticket. |
| `tickets[].brand_id` | integer | The id of the brand this ticket is associated with. |
| `tickets[].collaborator_ids` | array of integer | The ids of users currently CC'ed on the ticket. |
| `tickets[].collaborators` | array of object | POST requests only. Users to add as cc's when creating a ticket. |
| `tickets[].collaborators[].email` | string | Collaborator email. |
| `tickets[].collaborators[].name` | string | Collaborator name. |
| `tickets[].comment` | object | Write only. Adds a comment to the ticket. A ticket can contain up to 5000 comments; above this returns 422 when adding comments. |
| `tickets[].created_at` | string | When this record was created. |
| `tickets[].custom_fields` | array of object | Custom fields for the ticket. |
| `tickets[].custom_fields[].id` | integer | The id of the custom field. |
| `tickets[].custom_fields[].value` | string | The value of the custom field. |
| `tickets[].custom_status_id` | integer | The custom ticket status id of the ticket. |
| `tickets[].description` | string | Read-only first comment on the ticket. When creating a ticket, use `comment` to set the description. |
| `tickets[].due_at` | string | If type is `task`, the due date in ISO 8601 format. |
| `tickets[].email_cc_ids` | array of integer | IDs of agents or end users currently CC'ed on the ticket (ignored if CCs and followers not enabled). |
| `tickets[].email_ccs` | object | Write only. Represents email CCs to add/delete (ignored if CCs and followers not enabled). |
| `tickets[].encoded_id` | string | Encoded string representing the ticket's unique identifier. |
| `tickets[].external_id` | string | An id you can use to link Zendesk Support tickets to local records. |
| `tickets[].follower_ids` | array of integer | IDs of agents following the ticket (ignored if CCs and followers not enabled). |
| `tickets[].followers` | object | Write only. Represents agent followers to add/delete (ignored if CCs and followers not enabled). |
| `tickets[].followup_ids` | array of integer | IDs of followups created from this ticket (visible once ticket is closed). |
| `tickets[].forum_topic_id` | integer | Topic in the Zendesk Web portal this ticket originated from (portal is deprecated). |
| `tickets[].from_messaging_channel` | boolean | If true, the ticket’s via type is a messaging channel. |
| `tickets[].generated_timestamp` | integer | Unix timestamp representing the most accurate reading of when this record was last updated. |
| `tickets[].group_id` | integer | The group this ticket is assigned to. |
| `tickets[].has_incidents` | boolean | True if ticket is a `problem` and has one or more incidents linked to it. |
| `tickets[].id` | integer | Automatically assigned when the ticket is created. |
| `tickets[].is_public` | boolean | True if any comments are public, false otherwise. |
| `tickets[].macro_id` | integer | Write only. A macro ID to be recorded in the ticket audit. |
| `tickets[].macro_ids` | array of integer | POST requests only. List of macro IDs to be recorded in the ticket audit. |
| `tickets[].metadata` | object | Write only. Metadata for the audit (specified under `audit.custom` in the `metadata` object). |
| `tickets[].organization_id` | integer | Organization of the requester (must be associated with requester). |
| `tickets[].priority` | string | Urgency. Possible values: `urgent`, `high`, `normal`, `low`. |
| `tickets[].problem_id` | integer | For `incident` tickets, ID of the linked problem ticket. |
| `tickets[].raw_subject` | string | Dynamic content placeholder if present, otherwise the `subject`. |
| `tickets[].recipient` | string | Original recipient e-mail address of the ticket. Notification emails are sent from this address. |
| `tickets[].requester` | object | Write only. Requester object. |
| `tickets[].requester_id` | integer | The user who requested this ticket. (Marked required in the scraped field list.) |
| `tickets[].safe_update` | boolean | Write only. When true (and `update_stamp` included), protects against update collisions. False behaves like true; omit to force updates to not be safe. |
| `tickets[].satisfaction_rating` | object | Satisfaction rating object (schema not specified). |
| `tickets[].sharing_agreement_ids` | array of integer | IDs of sharing agreements used for this ticket. |
| `tickets[].status` | string | State. Possible values: `new`, `open`, `pending`, `hold`, `solved`, `closed`. If custom statuses are activated, this is the status category. |
| `tickets[].subject` | string | Subject field value. |
| `tickets[].submitter_id` | integer | User who submitted the ticket (author of first comment). |
| `tickets[].tags` | array of string | Tags applied to the ticket. Unless otherwise specified, set behavior overwrites and replaces existing tags. |
| `tickets[].ticket_form_id` | integer | Enterprise only. Ticket form id. |
| `tickets[].type` | string | Type. Possible values: `problem`, `incident`, `question`, `task`. |
| `tickets[].updated_at` | string | When record last got updated (only updated if update generates a ticket event). |
| `tickets[].updated_stamp` | string | Write only. Datetime of last update received from API (see `safe_update`). |
| `tickets[].url` | string | API url of this ticket. |
| `tickets[].via` | object | Via object describing how the ticket/event was created. |
| `tickets[].via.channel` | string | Channel (examples: `web`, `mobile`, `rule`, `system`). |
| `tickets[].via.source` | object | Source details (not further specified). |
| `tickets[].via_followup_source_id` | integer | POST requests only. ID of a closed ticket when creating a follow-up ticket. |
| `tickets[].via_id` | integer | Write only. Via identifier. |
| `tickets[].voice_comment` | object | Write only. Voice comment object. |

## Available Sorting Options

- `sort_by`: `id`, `subject`, `deleted_at`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, `status`, `requester`, `requester.name`, `group`, `assignee`, `assignee.name`
- `sort_order`: `asc` (default), `desc`
- `sort`: free-form field name; prefix with `-` for descending (especially relevant for cursor pagination)

## Sample Request

```bash
curl -i --request GET \
  'https://{{OAUTH_REQUEST_PAYLOAD.formData.ZENDESK_SUBDOMAIN}}.zendesk.com/api/v2/tickets?per_page=50&sort_by=created_at&sort_order=asc&include=users,groups' \
  --header 'Accept: application/json'
```

## Example Usage

### Example 1: Filter by external ID

```bash
curl -sS \
  'https://{{OAUTH_REQUEST_PAYLOAD.formData.ZENDESK_SUBDOMAIN}}.zendesk.com/api/v2/tickets?external_id=ext-001' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

### Example 2: Cursor pagination (next page)

```bash
curl -sS \
  'https://{{OAUTH_REQUEST_PAYLOAD.formData.ZENDESK_SUBDOMAIN}}.zendesk.com/api/v2/tickets?page%5Bsize%5D=50&page%5Bafter%5D=eyJvIjoiaWQiLCJ2IjoiYVFFPSJ9&sort=-created_at' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

### Example 3: Incremental-style filter using `start_time`

```bash
curl -sS \
  'https://{{OAUTH_REQUEST_PAYLOAD.formData.ZENDESK_SUBDOMAIN}}.zendesk.com/api/v2/tickets?start_time=1332034771' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

## Notes

- `include` accepts a comma-separated list of sideloads (for example: `users,groups,organizations`).
- `page` supports both integer paging and cursor paging (deepObject); use only one style per request.
